hero.headline: Supreme Court allows border wall construction in Texas Big Bend region in 8-1 ruling
hero.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 on Monday to allow the Trump administration to proceed with border wall construction in the Big Bend region of southwest Texas, lifting a lower court in
hero.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 on Monday to allow the Trump administration to proceed with border wall construction in the Big Bend region of southwest Texas, lifting a lower court injunction that had halted the project. The court found that the federal judge who blocked construction lacked authority to do so and said the administration was extremely likely to prevail on that issue. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the lone dissenter.

The dispute centers on three waivers issued by Homeland Security secretaries Kristi Noem and Markwayne Mullin between February and July that allow the government to bypass environmental and conservation laws for the project. The planned construction covers 341 miles in the sparsely populated area along the Rio Grande, including parts of Big Bend National Park. The administration said 89,000 people have been detained attempting to cross there in recent years.

District Judge Kathleen Cardone had invalidated the waivers in October, ruling that the Homeland Security secretary lacked such broad powers under a 1996 law. The administration argued that Congress granted it wide authority to build border infrastructure without regulatory delays. The Supreme Court said the government has compelling interests when border security policies are challenged.

The case was brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, Friends of the Ruidosa Church, and a local property owner who argued construction would permanently damage the landscape and threaten historic and cultural sites. They contended the Big Bend area has the lowest migrant apprehension rates along the southern border, making the waivers inappropriate. Government data confirms Big Bend has the fewest encounters between federal agents and migrants of any border section. The administration has said completing the wall there is necessary to prevent the area from becoming an entry point if other sections are built.

cards.headline: Krakow mass shooting suspect dies in hospital as Polish prosecutors say motive investigation continues
cards.teaser: The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Pol
cards.body:
The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Polish man was shot by police officers within three minutes of opening fire in the city's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon. He had been hospitalized with injuries sustained during a gunfight with responding officers.

Polish prosecutors said Monday that investigations into the suspect's motive remain ongoing, walking back earlier statements by a government minister who described the gunman as inspired by far-right ideologies and ultra-nationalism. Przemysław Nowak, a spokesperson for Poland's National Prosecutor's Office, told reporters the motive inquiry continues. The suspect has not been officially named.

The attack killed four Polish citizens, a British national, and an Austrian woman in the Main Market Square. Police later found three bodies at the gunman's home, identified as his 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother, and 21-year-old sister. Authorities seized four firearms from the suspect's car, including two AR-15 rifles and two handguns, along with several hundred rounds of ammunition. Polish media reported the suspect held a firearms permit.

Sixteen people were hospitalized after the shooting, including two police officers who were injured during the gunfight with the suspect. A surgeon who was eating nearby when the attack began rushed to the scene and helped treat victims before ambulances arrived. Professor Michał Pędziwiatr said his colleague used his hand to stem bleeding from a severely injured police officer, and that intervention undoubtedly saved the officer's life. Both wounded officers have since emerged from comas.

Poland declared two days of national mourning following the attack. Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited Krakow and said the country had not previously experienced such drastic terrorism.

cards.headline: ICE detains 8-year-old Haitian boy at routine check-in after TPS termination, prompting San Diego school district response
cards.teaser: Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him
cards.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him to federal custody, according to school officials and an advocacy group. The boy, a third grader at Fay Elementary School, lost his Temporary Protected Status protections this summer after a Supreme Court decision allowed President Donald Trump to end TPS for Haitians. He was summoned to meet with ICE officers Wednesday, and his uncle brought him to the appointment to comply with the law, according to a letter San Diego Unified School District officials sent Friday to the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Health and Human Services.

ICE officers determined the boy to be an unaccompanied minor after the uncle could not establish legal guardianship, according to a DHS spokesperson. The agency said it removed the boy from the household out of caution to ensure his safety. The boy was subsequently transferred to the Office of Refugee Resettlement, which takes custody of children deemed unaccompanied minors. As of Monday, his family did not know where he was being held, according to Representative Juan Vargas.

The boy had been living with his uncle and cousins after his father was deported last year, according to the school district and the Haitian Bridge Alliance, an immigrant rights advocacy group. TPS is a humanitarian designation that had shielded hundreds of thousands of Haitians from deportation following the country's 2010 earthquake. The protections were renewed multiple times as Haiti descended into crisis, with gangs now controlling much of the capital after the president was assassinated in 2021.

The school district said it is sending crisis counselors to Fay Elementary School this week because the boy's classmates have expressed concern and fear for him. School officials asked DHS and HHS to reconsider how immigration enforcement policies are affecting students, but as of Monday had received no response. The Office of Refugee Resettlement said it does not comment on specific cases. The boy is among 1,640 children considered unaccompanied minors currently in HHS care.

cards.headline: Qantas to outsource 850 jobs to Accenture, most moving to India
cards.teaser: Qantas will outsource 850 corporate jobs to consulting firm Accenture, with most of the positions moving to India, as the Australian airline accelerates investment in artificial in
cards.body:
Qantas will outsource 850 corporate jobs to consulting firm Accenture, with most of the positions moving to India, as the Australian airline accelerates investment in artificial intelligence and information technology modernization. Chief Executive Vanessa Hudson announced the plan in an internal email to staff on Tuesday, saying the job cuts will begin in mid-2027.

The outsourcing will start with finance, procurement, human resources, and marketing roles shifting mostly to teams in India and some to Australia. Hudson said the airline is seeking to modernize its IT systems and cited the rapid pace of technological change. Qantas spends more than 1 billion Australian dollars annually on technology and operates more than 1,000 legacy applications that were not designed to work together, she said.

Under the multi-year deal with Accenture, Qantas aims to redesign and simplify corporate functions and reduce duplication so staff can focus on work that creates value for customers and the business, Hudson said. The company said the work transferred to Accenture will eventually be transformed further with automation and artificial intelligence.

Qantas employs approximately 28,000 staff in Australia and 4,000 globally. The announcement comes days after the airline issued a market update indicating fare increases and flight reductions due to higher fuel costs. Hudson acknowledged the difficulty of the news, telling staff she was sorry for the uncertainty it brings. The airline said it is in talks with unions and staff on the plans.

cards.headline: Wyndham exposed millions of customer records after hardcoded password found in Android app
cards.teaser: Hotel giant Wyndham acknowledged a security incident after a researcher discovered a hardcoded password in its Android app that granted access to an internal database containing pe
cards.body:
Hotel giant Wyndham acknowledged a security incident after a researcher discovered a hardcoded password in its Android app that granted access to an internal database containing personal information for millions of rewards members. Security researcher Robert Wiggins found the credential embedded in the app's source code, which allowed access to a Salesforce-hosted database storing customer names, email addresses, member numbers, and login tokens.

The database contained millions of entries from Wyndham's 129 million enrolled rewards members, though Wiggins could not determine an exact count of exposed records. The credential was revoked after Wiggins contacted Wyndham through a journalist because the company had no public channel for reporting security vulnerabilities. A Wyndham spokesperson said the company addressed the issue and found no evidence of unauthorized access, but declined to say whether server logs existed to verify that claim.

Wyndham would not disclose how long the password was embedded in the app, whether it plans to notify affected customers, or whether it will report the incident to the Securities and Exchange Commission as required for material cybersecurity events at public companies. Hardcoded credentials are considered a critical security weakness because anyone with the software can extract and use the password, and such vulnerabilities typically receive maximum severity ratings.

This marks the second major discovery of hardcoded credentials by Wiggins in two weeks, following a similar flaw in the Applebee's app. Wiggins used artificial intelligence tools to scan decompiled app code for such weaknesses. Wyndham's cybersecurity director provided an email address for researchers to report issues, but the company declined to say whether it would establish a formal vulnerability disclosure program or update its website to publicize the reporting channel.

Wyndham experienced a separate security incident in 2024 when hotel check-in computers were found running remote-access spyware that leaked guest records to the internet. That spyware company was later hacked and shut down, and its owner was convicted of making and selling unlawful spyware.

cards.headline: Reds first baseman Sal Stewart wins NL Rookie of the Year after 32-homer, 112-RBI season
cards.teaser: Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart won the National League Rookie of the Year award, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced Monday. Stewart received 20 of 30
cards.body:
Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart won the National League Rookie of the Year award, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced Monday. Stewart received 20 of 30 first-place votes and was the only player in the NL field to appear in the top five on every ballot. The award also earns Cincinnati a bonus pick after the first round of the 2027 draft through the Prospect Promotion Incentive.

Stewart led NL rookies with 700 plate appearances and hit .263/.330/.457 with 32 home runs and 112 RBI. His home run total was 12 more than any other rookie in the league, while his RBI count was nearly 40 ahead of any other first-year player. He finished eighth in the NL in home runs and trailed only Cardinals first baseman Alec Burleson in RBI among all league hitters. Stewart started 110 games at first base, 33 at third base, 11 as a designated hitter, and seven at second base.

Mets outfielder Carson Benge finished second with seven first-place votes and Cardinals middle infielder JJ Wetherholt placed third with three first-place votes. Benge hit .282/.346/.430 with a 20-20 season and was one of the best hitters in the NL after the All-Star Break. Wetherholt appeared to be Stewart's top competition for much of the season but struggled in the second half around a two-week absence due to right wrist tendinitis. Both Benge and Wetherholt were Gold Glove finalists at their positions.

Park adjustments for Cincinnati's hitter-friendly stadium and Stewart's lack of defensive value limited his standing in advanced metrics. Both FanGraphs and Baseball Reference graded Stewart at two wins above replacement, about half the totals for Benge and Wetherholt. The majority of voters prioritized Stewart's power production. All three finalists met Prospect Promotion Incentive criteria and opened the year on their teams' MLB rosters, meaning the winner would secure a bonus pick. Stewart is the Reds' second Rookie of the Year winner this decade and ninth in franchise history.

cards.headline: Donnie Dunagan, voice of Bambi in 1942 Disney classic, dies at 92
cards.teaser: Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.
cards.body:
Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.

Dunagan's brief acting career spanned just seven films over a few years but included two enduring roles. At age four, he made his film debut in 1938's Mother Carey's Chickens. In 1939, he starred in Son of Frankenstein alongside Boris Karloff and Bela Lugosi, playing the son of Baron Wolf von Frankenstein. Walt Disney personally selected Dunagan to be the facial model for Bambi because of his brown eyes, having animators sketch his expressions before offering him the voice role. Dunagan later called the work the thrill of his young life.

After his acting career ended, Dunagan volunteered for the Marines in the early 1950s and served 21 years, including combat in the Korean and Vietnam wars. He earned a Bronze Star and Purple Heart and rose to the rank of major. He kept his Bambi role secret throughout his military service, fearing it would undermine his authority. He said in 2005 that if the troops he led had found out about Bambi, they would have ridden him out on a rail.

Disney tracked Dunagan down in the early 2000s for a DVD release of Bambi, returning him to public life. He became a Disney ambassador and appeared at fan conventions. His agents said Dunagan loved his fans, rallied other veterans, and had an infectious smile and warmth that never lost the childlike spirit of his acting youth.

cards.headline: Paraguay formally charges ousted president Santiago Peña with breach of trust over Ueno Bank collapse
cards.teaser: Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.
cards.body:
Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.

Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the digital bank's demise, which has left more than half of Paraguay's population—an estimated three million depositors—unable to access their savings and pensions. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028.

cards.body:
The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.

The 25-year-old Polish man drove into the square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car, killing four women and two men including a British national before armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes. A minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by far-right ideologies and described him as an ultra-nationalist.

Committee Chair James Comer said Epstein operated with impunity, shielded by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims.

Nvidia's board of directors announced Sunday that it is opening an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and hours later President Donald Trump publicly defended Huang, calling him an honorable guy who has done an amazing job for the country.

Google DeepMind researchers used agentic artificial intelligence to mathematically prove a number of the Signal protocol's key cryptographic guarantees, marking a development for b

The researchers completed the project in four weeks using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code, according to a report published Tuesday. The analysis serves as independent validation of the cryptography that protects communications on platforms including the Signal app, Google Messages, and WhatsApp.

cards.headline: NRC grants X-energy construction permit for four small modular reactors at Texas Dow plant
cards.teaser: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has approved a construction permit for X-energy to build four small modular reactors at a Dow chemical plant in Texas, the nuclear startup announc
cards.body:
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has approved a construction permit for X-energy to build four small modular reactors at a Dow chemical plant in Texas, the nuclear startup announc

The permit marks the first approval for an advanced nuclear reactor at an industrial site in the United States. Each of the four Xe-100 reactors will be capable of generating 80 megawatts of electricity and 200 megawatts of heat, though the reactors are not expected to be operational until the early 2030s.

cards.headline: Researchers trace mysterious global power grid frequency drops to synchronized battery backup systems
cards.teaser: Researchers at Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany have solved a years-long mystery that has troubled grid managers worldwide: unexplained frequency drops occurring every 60 second
cards.body:
Researchers at Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany have solved a years-long mystery that has troubled grid managers worldwide: unexplained frequency drops occurring every 60 second

The culprit is battery backup systems, including those in data centers, that check their charge status at precisely the same time every minute due to internet-synchronized clocks. Director Dirk Witthaut led the investigation after Germany's largest transmission system operator, Tennet Germany, brought the puzzle to his team.

cards.headline: Meta expands AI age detection for Instagram teen accounts worldwide after $17.1 billion settlement
cards.teaser: Meta is expanding the artificial intelligence technology it uses to identify teenagers on Instagram who have not correctly disclosed their age to users worldwide. The rollout, anno
cards.body:
Meta is expanding the artificial intelligence technology it uses to identify teenagers on Instagram who have not correctly disclosed their age to users worldwide. The rollout, anno

The rollout, announced Sunday, will automatically place millions more teens into Instagram Teen Account protections after launching in the United States, European Union, and Brazil last year. The expansion follows a $17.1 billion lawsuit settlement in August in which Meta agreed to strengthen its age assurance practices and impose stricter restrictions on teen users.

cards.headline: AI tools are enabling automated hacking at scale, upending the cybersecurity industry
cards.teaser: Artificial intelligence systems are now enabling attackers to automate the entire hacking process in real time, fundamentally disrupting the cybersecurity industry built over the p
cards.body:
Artificial intelligence systems are now enabling attackers to automate the entire hacking process in real time, fundamentally disrupting the cybersecurity industry built over the p

Open-weight AI models have advanced to the point where they can automatically identify software vulnerabilities, write exploits, and break into targets simultaneously, collapsing what was traditionally a multi-step process requiring teams of skilled hackers. Stamos described a wave of breaches in recent weeks affecting major technology companies, including a chain of attacks that began with a compromise of Fireworks, an AI services provider.

hero.headline: Reds first baseman Sal Stewart wins NL Rookie of the Year after 32-homer, 112-RBI season
hero.teaser: Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart won the National League Rookie of the Year award, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced Monday. Stewart received 20 of 30
hero.body:
Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart won the National League Rookie of the Year award, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced Monday. Stewart received 20 of 30 first-place votes and was the only player in the NL field to appear in the top five on every ballot. The award also earns Cincinnati a bonus pick after the first round of the 2027 draft through the Prospect Promotion Incentive.

Stewart led NL rookies with 700 plate appearances and hit .263/.330/.457 with 32 home runs and 112 RBI. His home run total was 12 more than any other rookie in the league, while his RBI count was nearly 40 ahead of any other first-year player. He finished eighth in the NL in home runs and trailed only Cardinals first baseman Alec Burleson in RBI among all league hitters. Stewart started 110 games at first base, 33 at third base, 11 as a designated hitter, and seven at second base.

Mets outfielder Carson Benge finished second with seven first-place votes and Cardinals middle infielder JJ Wetherholt placed third with three first-place votes. Benge hit .282/.346/.430 with a 20-20 season and was one of the best hitters in the NL after the All-Star Break. Wetherholt appeared to be Stewart's top competition for much of the season but struggled in the second half around a two-week absence due to right wrist tendinitis. Both Benge and Wetherholt were Gold Glove finalists at their positions.

Park adjustments for Cincinnati's hitter-friendly stadium and Stewart's lack of defensive value limited his standing in advanced metrics. Both FanGraphs and Baseball Reference graded Stewart at two wins above replacement, about half the totals for Benge and Wetherholt. The majority of voters prioritized Stewart's power production. All three finalists met Prospect Promotion Incentive criteria and opened the year on their teams' MLB rosters, meaning the winner would secure a bonus pick. Stewart is the Reds' second Rookie of the Year winner this decade and ninth in franchise history.

cards.headline: Bills join 49ers atop NFL at 7-1 as season reaches midpoint

The Buffalo Bills moved to 7-1 on Monday with a 23-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings, joining the San Francisco 49ers at the top of the NFL standings as the regular season reach

The Bills defense limited Minnesota quarterback Carson Wentz to eight completions on 25 attempts before he was benched in the fourth quarter. The Vikings dropped to 6-2 and fell from first to third in the NFC North, where all four teams now have at least six wins.

cards.headline: Vikings acquire Kirk Cousins from Raiders in trade deadline deal
cards.teaser: The Minnesota Vikings have acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick, Yahoo Sports confirmed Tuesday. The trade reunites
cards.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick, Yahoo Sports confirmed Tuesday. The trade reunites

The trade reunites Cousins with the franchise where he last started in 2023 and addresses Minnesota's struggling quarterback situation following Carson Wentz's three-turnover, 81-yard performance in a Week 9 loss to Buffalo. Cousins, 38, has completed his best season in years with the Raiders, throwing 20 touchdowns against eight interceptions through nine games.

cards.headline: Kenneth Walker scores three touchdowns as Chiefs defeat Jets 35-12, Mahomes plays through elbow injury
cards.teaser: Kenneth Walker scored three touchdowns as the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the New York Jets 35-12 on Sunday, snapping a two-game losing streak. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes t
cards.body:
Kenneth Walker scored three touchdowns as the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the New York Jets 35-12 on Sunday, snapping a two-game losing streak. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes t

Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns despite playing through a right elbow injury sustained on a second-quarter strip-sack by Jets defensive lineman David Bailey that left his arm bent at an awkward angle. Mahomes flexed his elbow on the sideline, threw warmup passes, and returned to the game, though he received treatment from Chiefs trainer Julie Frymyer at halftime and planned additional testing afterward.

cards.headline: Blades Brown, 19, becomes youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years with playoff victory in Mexico
cards.teaser: Blades Brown became the youngest winner on the PGA Tour in 95 years after defeating Ben James in a playoff at the World Wide Technology Championship in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. Brow
cards.body:
Blades Brown became the youngest winner on the PGA Tour in 95 years after defeating Ben James in a playoff at the World Wide Technology Championship in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. Brow

Brown, at 19 years and 171 days old, beat his fellow American on the second playoff hole after shooting a nine-under-par 63 in the final round, which included a birdie on the 18th hole to complete a comeback from seven shots behind. Brown is the youngest PGA Tour winner since 18-year-old Charles Kocsis won the 1931 Michigan Open, which was considered a regional event in the early years of the tour.

The Jaguars will send a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to New Orleans for Godchaux, according to multiple reports. Godchaux appeared in all eight Saints games this season, making five starts before moving to a reserve role over the final three contests.

cards.headline: Willy Hutchinson upsets Joshua Buatsi to win WBC light-heavyweight title in Manchester rematch

cards.body:
Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship Saturday night in Manchester, defeating Joshua Buatsi by decision to avenge a loss from 2024. The judges scored the rema

The judges scored the rematch 117-112, 115-113, 115-113 in favor of Hutchinson, making the 28-year-old Scot the first British champion at the weight since Nathan Cleverly in 2017. The bout was elevated from an interim title fight to a full championship after American David Benavidez vacated the belt to move up to cruiserweight.

hero.headline: Donnie Dunagan, voice of Bambi in 1942 Disney classic, dies at 92
hero.teaser: Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.
hero.body:
Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.

Dunagan's brief acting career spanned just seven films over a few years but included two enduring roles. At age four, he made his film debut in 1938's Mother Carey's Chickens. In 1939, he starred in Son of Frankenstein alongside Boris Karloff and Bela Lugosi, playing the son of Baron Wolf von Frankenstein. Walt Disney personally selected Dunagan to be the facial model for Bambi because of his brown eyes, having animators sketch his expressions before offering him the voice role. Dunagan later called the work the thrill of his young life.

After his acting career ended, Dunagan volunteered for the Marines in the early 1950s and served 21 years, including combat in the Korean and Vietnam wars. He earned a Bronze Star and Purple Heart and rose to the rank of major. He kept his Bambi role secret throughout his military service, fearing it would undermine his authority. He said in 2005 that if the troops he led had found out about Bambi, they would have ridden him out on a rail.

Disney tracked Dunagan down in the early 2000s for a DVD release of Bambi, returning him to public life. He became a Disney ambassador and appeared at fan conventions. His agents said Dunagan loved his fans, rallied other veterans, and had an infectious smile and warmth that never lost the childlike spirit of his acting youth.

M. John Harrison has become the oldest ever winner of the Booker Prize, receiving the prestigious literary award for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything. Harrison, 81,

Harrison, 81, was named the winner of the £50,000 prize at a ceremony in London on Monday, surpassing Margaret Atwood as the oldest recipient in the award's history. The End of Everything is set in the years after a mysterious catastrophe that caused British society to collapse.

cards.body:
Director Denis Villeneuve said Saturday that he is putting final touches on the 70mm Imax print of Dune: Part Three while simultaneously starting work on his James Bond film. Speak

Speaking at the LACMA Art and Film Gala in Los Angeles, where he was honored, Villeneuve called the third Dune installment a very personal project and the completion of 10 years of work in the desert. Villeneuve declined to comment on Bond casting speculation on the red carpet, saying every word would be scrutinized, but added that he is having a great time.

cards.headline: Russell Brand sentencing hearing underway after rape and sexual assault convictions
cards.teaser: A sentencing hearing for Russell Brand is underway at Southwark Crown Court in London, where prosecutors are seeking a 10 to 15 year prison term for rape and sexual assault convict
cards.body:
A sentencing hearing for Russell Brand is underway at Southwark Crown Court in London, where prosecutors are seeking a 10 to 15 year prison term for rape and sexual assault convict

Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC called for a serious category one sentence, arguing Brand abused his position and degraded and humiliated his victims. Karmy-Jones told the judge that Brand held the view he could abuse without impunity and must bear responsibility for the culture around him that enabled his offending for years.

cards.body:
James Gunn and Peter Safran have been removed as co-CEOs and chairmen of DC Studios after four years leading the comic book film division, throwing the future of Superman, Batman,

Marvel veteran Jeremy Latcham, who produced superhero films including Iron Man, The Avengers, and Spider-Man: Homecoming, will take over leadership of the studio. Gunn and Safran launched a rebooted DC Universe in 2025 with Superman, starring David Corenswet as the Man of Steel, which earned $618 million worldwide.

cards.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero heads toward $32 million opening weekend, surpassing predecessor's total domestic run
cards.teaser: Godzilla Minus Zero is tracking toward a $32 million domestic box office debut, far exceeding the full theatrical run of its 2023 predecessor. The sequel, which centers on postwar
cards.body:
Godzilla Minus Zero is tracking toward a $32 million domestic box office debut, far exceeding the full theatrical run of its 2023 predecessor. The sequel, which centers on postwar

The sequel, which centers on postwar Japan dealing with attacks from the three-headed Ghidorah and the possibility of Godzilla's return, is outpacing Godzilla Minus One, which opened in December 2023 with $11.4 million and finished its domestic run at $57.1 million. The film holds a 90 percent critics approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

hero.headline: Van Hollen declines to rule out challenging Schumer for Senate Democratic leader as caucus debates strategy
hero.teaser: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode abou
hero.body:
Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode about a potential bid. Van Hollen said the party should not have a coronation and that he has not shut the door on a challenge to Schumer, who is currently minority leader and widely expected to be elected to lead the new Senate majority in January.

Van Hollen's comments come as some Senate Democrats have withheld support for Schumer while seeking clarity on the party's strategy for the next two years. Democrats are scheduled to meet as a group Tuesday to discuss their path forward. Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, who met with Van Hollen on Monday, said she will not vote for a majority leader candidate who cannot articulate a plan, especially for the first 100 days. Slotkin declined over the weekend to rule out her own leadership ambitions.

Both Van Hollen and Slotkin are viewed as potential presidential contenders. Van Hollen had previously suggested his focus was on 2028 and ensuring Democrats win back the White House.

Schumer needs only a majority of the Democratic caucus to win the leadership election during a closed-door meeting scheduled for early December. Many Senate Democrats have expressed support for Schumer following the party's performance in last week's midterm elections. Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut said Monday he plans to continue supporting Schumer but added that the Senate needs new ideas, energy from incoming members, and changes in how it operates.

cards.headline: Seven Republican senators call for delay in GOP leadership elections
cards.teaser: Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections
cards.body:
Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections

The elections are scheduled for Tuesday, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota is still expected to be reelected to lead the Senate GOP. Senators Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, Rick Scott of Florida, Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, and John Kennedy of Louisiana signed a letter demanding the elections be delayed to allow more discussion about the party's performance last week.

cards.headline: DeSantis positions for 2028 presidential run as Rubio deflects speculation following GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid
cards.body:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid

The maneuvering by both Florida Republicans underscores volatility in the early stages of the 2028 primary, where Vice President Vance had been viewed as a likely frontrunner before Tuesday's election results. DeSantis, whose term as governor ends in January, has fueled speculation through a postelection media campaign that included appearances on podcasts and CNN.

cards.headline: Elon Musk's companies face Democratic investigations after $475 million midterm spending resulted in losses
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4
cards.body:
Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4

Armed with subpoena power, Democrats are preparing to examine Musk's Department of Government Efficiency operation, its access to sensitive government data, and whether his companies benefited from his influence over the Trump administration. More than 99 percent of Musk's traceable spending went to losing candidates, according to WIRED.

cards.headline: Jeffries pushes to restrict China chip exports in defense bill
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C

Jeffries told reporters he strongly supports measures currently in the Senate version of the National Defense Authorization Act that would restrict chip access to China and will push to ensure those provisions make it into the final legislation. Jeffries spoke a day after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

cards.headline: House Republicans weigh impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth this week over alleged illegal continuation of Iran war
cards.teaser: House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing
cards.body:
House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing

The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began. Speaker Mike Johnson had canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early before Election Day to avoid the politically difficult impeachment measure.

cards.headline: Attorney General dismisses Calley Means' White House corruption allegations as former FDA chief backs some claims
cards.teaser: Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday dismissed corruption allegations made by former Trump health adviser Calley Means against senior White House officials, calling Means a disg
cards.body:
Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday dismissed corruption allegations made by former Trump health adviser Calley Means against senior White House officials, calling Means a disg

Blanche told CNN he would not investigate claims Means made on a podcast, even as former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary corroborated aspects of the allegations and Representative Marlin Stutzman, an Indiana Republican, said any impropriety claims should be examined. Means alleged in a Friday interview that former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles blocked an initiative to examine children's sugar consumption because she wanted sugar industry donations for midterm elections.
